title: Umbra VPN
summary: Distributed VPN platform with automated access, subscriptions and node orchestration
description: A privately operated, revenue-generating VPN service serving an existing user base. Umbra VPN is an actively deployed product rather than only a technical exercise: operating it includes managing subscriptions and infrastructure, supporting customers, resolving production issues, and improving reliability in response to real usage.

The platform manages a fleet of independently deployed VPN nodes from a central control plane written in Rust. Its core service exposes an HTTP API with Axum, persists accounts, access entitlements, subscriptions, and usage state in PostgreSQL, and issues commands to node-side agents over gRPC using Tonic and shared Protocol Buffers contracts. A Telegram bot built with Teloxide provides self-service onboarding, account management, connection setup, subscription changes, notifications, and separate operator workflows.

Each node agent manages credentials, service health, connection details, and usage collection close to the VPN engine it controls. Mutual TLS authenticates and encrypts control-plane communication between machines, while containerized deployments and automated build and deployment workflows keep the distributed services reproducible. Provider-specific, payment, and security-sensitive operational details remain private.
highlights: revenue-generating service operated for a real user base
distributed rust control plane and independently deployed node agents
automated access, subscription, usage and support workflows

title: Cogniflex
summary: Research-driven platform for detecting AI-generated text, images and video
description: An open-source team project for detecting and explaining AI-generated text, images, and video through complementary static and model-based analysis. Cogniflex is designed to return probabilistic assessments with supporting evidence instead of presenting uncertain detector output as an absolute verdict. Manual submission and an in-browser workflow are being developed so people can inspect content without leaving the page they are reading.

The static-analysis engine is implemented in Java and evaluates deterministic signals such as prompt or assistant leakage, characteristic vocabulary and formatting, stylometric measurements, invisible Unicode characters, watermark patterns, provenance metadata, and generator-specific media artifacts. Each rule reports concrete evidence with its own confidence, severity, and weight, allowing the orchestration layer to combine weak and strong indicators while keeping the result explainable.

Model-based detection is separated into a Python inference service responsible for preprocessing, model loading, and inference paths for supported media types. A Spring Boot backend exposes REST and OpenAPI interfaces, coordinates the analysis pipeline, and communicates with the ML service over gRPC using shared Protocol Buffers contracts. PostgreSQL stores analysis history, Redis supports infrastructure concerns such as rate limiting, and React and TypeScript clients provide the website and browser-extension interfaces.

The project includes research notebooks, configurable rules, locale-aware text preprocessing, Docker Compose environments, and tests across rules, preprocessing, orchestration, controllers, and service integration. The architecture and research foundation are implemented incrementally; real-time browser analysis and broader image and video coverage remain active development areas rather than finished claims.
highlights: hybrid explainable rule engine and machine-learning pipeline
spring boot and python services connected through grpc
research into linguistic, watermark, provenance and media artifacts

title: Claude Usage Tray
summary: Linux tray app for monitoring Claude limits, reset times and usage credits
description: An unofficial, lightweight Linux tray application that keeps Claude subscription usage visible without opening another window. It reports five-hour and weekly limits, reset times, plan details, and optional credit balances by polling Anthropic's API with credentials from an existing Claude CLI or desktop login. The application registers through the desktop-environment-agnostic D-Bus Status Notifier protocol, works across window managers, supports TOML-based display and polling configuration, and includes commands for installing its desktop entry and systemd user service.
highlights: desktop-environment-agnostic tray integration over d-bus
configurable usage, reset and credit reporting
cargo installation with desktop and systemd service setup

title: C Macro Helper
summary: Published VS Code extension for formatting multiline C and C++ macros
description: A published Visual Studio Code extension that removes the repetitive formatting work from multiline C and C++ macros. Its editor commands add and vertically align continuation backslashes for a selection or the macro under the cursor, with a separate finalize command that leaves the last line plain and a configurable alignment gap for consistent formatting. The extension is distributed through the Visual Studio Marketplace and GitHub releases, integrates with the command palette, editor context menu, and keyboard shortcuts, and is backed by automated tests and a GitHub Actions workflow.
highlights: published on the visual studio marketplace
selection-aware macro detection and backslash alignment
configurable formatting with automated tests and ci

title: Cinema Management Database
summary: PostgreSQL cinema system with reservations, pricing, roles and lifecycle rules
description: A complete PostgreSQL database design for operating a cinema chain, covering locations, halls, seats, films, customers, screenings, reservations, and tickets. Its relational model and constraints keep the core domain consistent, including non-overlapping screenings within a hall and one reservation for each seat at a particular screening.

Business rules live directly in PL/pgSQL functions, procedures, triggers, and views. The database calculates ticket prices, validates ticket and reservation lifecycles, supports scheduling and cancellation workflows, and exposes reporting-oriented views. It also defines separate customer, organizer, manager, and administrator roles, and ships ordered initialization scripts, generated test data, rollback-safe tests, and cross-platform backup scripts.
highlights: database-enforced screening, reservation and ticket rules
functions, procedures, triggers and reporting views
four-role access model with tests and backup tooling

title: Qt Chat App
summary: Cross-platform Qt 6 chat system with raw TCP, accounts, groups and PostgreSQL
description: A complete client-server messaging system built from the ground up in C++20 and Qt 6 rather than on top of an existing chat or networking framework. Communication runs directly over TCP using a custom application protocol with purpose-built packet types, framing, serialization, and transport abstractions. A shared protocol library defines how the client and server encode, transmit, validate, and reconstruct packets and data objects without coupling network code to the interface or business logic.

The concurrent server manages registration, authentication, profiles, connection state, private conversations, groups, message history, and disconnection handling. PostgreSQL persists users, chats, memberships, content, messages, and user statistics. Ordered migrations add lifecycle triggers, private-chat creation, message search, and statistics maintenance so database behavior evolves alongside the application.

The QML desktop client implements account onboarding, profiles, private and group conversations, message history, and network-state feedback. Client, server, protocol, persistence, and interface code live in dedicated components, making it possible to extend operations without rewriting the whole stack.

CMake presets and a Justfile support Windows, Linux, and macOS builds, while Docker Compose packages the server with PostgreSQL. GoogleTest suites, GitHub Actions, architecture diagrams, and generated Doxygen documentation support verification and maintenance. Although it began as a university assignment, it was developed as a substantial passion project and functional product rather than a minimal demonstration.
highlights: custom tcp packet protocol shared by qt client and server
accounts, private chats, groups and persistent message history
cross-platform builds, docker deployment, tests and generated docs

title: Databoxer
summary: Cross-platform CLI that encrypts files into a custom .box container format
description: A cross-platform command-line encryption utility for protecting local files, removable media, and data in transit on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Databoxer uses ChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption with randomly generated 32-byte keys and a unique nonce per file, providing confidentiality and integrity while storing encrypted content and optional encrypted metadata in a custom `.box` container.

A profile system lets users maintain multiple password-protected encryption identities and explicitly manage their keys. The CLI accepts multiple files or directories, supports recursive processing and custom destinations, and restores original names during decryption when metadata is available. The beta is published on crates.io, distributed through platform-specific release builds, and verified by CI across the supported operating systems; native keyring integration, compression, archives, and a GUI remain planned work.
highlights: chacha20-poly1305 authenticated encryption with per-file nonces
custom .box containers and password-protected profiles
published cross-platform cli with automated release builds

title: Copper
summary: Single-file build system for C and C++, simpler than CMake or large Makefiles
description: An early-stage build system created to make C and C++ project configuration more direct than CMake, large Makefiles, or Visual Studio solutions. Copper reads a single `copper.yaml` file, discovers source files automatically, and translates project settings into compilation and linking steps for GCC, Clang, and MSVC while still exposing compiler flags, include paths, target directories, and other build controls.

Projects are divided into independently configurable units, comparable to projects within a Visual Studio solution, that can produce binaries, static libraries, or dynamic libraries. The Rust CLI can initialize a project, generate example configuration, add units, and build the whole project or selected targets. Copper is usable from the current source tree but has no stable release yet, and its configuration and interfaces remain subject to change.
highlights: single yaml configuration file per project
automatic source discovery and compiler orchestration
modular units for binaries and static or dynamic libraries

title: Signsense
summary: Android app translating Russian finger spelling with on-device ML
description: An Android app that translates Russian dactyl finger spelling into readable text through the phone's live camera feed. A custom-trained machine-learning model recognizes individual hand signs on-device, assembles them into words, detects pauses between words, and presents a running translation without a network round trip.

The translator works with front and rear cameras, includes a low-light flashlight control, and provides recognition settings, light and dark themes, and English and Russian interface languages. The released APK targets Android 8 through 12 and currently recognizes Russian dactyl only; ASL support and a broader rewrite were ideas for future work, not shipped features. The project began as a school project, with the application developed by me and model training handled by a dedicated contributor.
highlights: custom-trained gesture recognition model
on-device camera inference with word-boundary detection
released android application built by a two-person team

title: Pasteshelf
summary: Pastebin-style REST backend with accounts, hash IDs and PostgreSQL
description: A lightweight Pastebin-inspired Spring Boot backend where registered users create, edit, store, and share text pastes identified by unique hash IDs. Its REST API implements the paste CRUD lifecycle, public reads, account ownership, and HTTP Basic authentication, with PostgreSQL persistence and Flyway-managed schema migrations. Custom domain exceptions are handled through a global API error layer, and endpoint integration tests verify the main workflows. The service can run through Gradle against an existing database or as a Docker Compose stack with a preconfigured PostgreSQL container.
highlights: unique hash ids for shareable pastes
account authentication and paste ownership
flyway migrations, integration tests and docker compose

title: Bybit Trading Bot
summary: Bybit P2P automation with a reverse-engineered Payeer payment integration
description: A freelance automation service that reduced manual work across Bybit P2P order processing and Payeer payment execution. It monitored incoming and outgoing orders through Bybit's official API, extracted the transaction data required for each workflow, and coordinated payment completion through an asynchronous Rust pipeline built on Tokio.

Payeer did not expose the interface required by the project, so its web flow was reconstructed into a private integration covering endpoint behavior, authenticated sessions, CSRF handling, and request-signature generation. The result demonstrates reliable orchestration across documented and reverse-engineered third-party systems while keeping client-specific business rules, credentials, and operational details private.
highlights: reverse-engineered payeer web integration
session, csrf token and request-signature handling
asynchronous order and payment orchestration with tokio

title: Feather Chat
summary: Multithreaded TCP chat prototype built directly on Java sockets
description: An early-stage Java client-server chat prototype built directly on TCP sockets to study networking and multithreaded message handling without a networking framework. The implemented version accepts multiple simultaneous clients and routes real-time broadcast messages through a central server. Direct user-to-user messages, chat rooms, account authentication, end-to-end encryption, and a desktop interface were planned but not completed before the project was archived.
highlights: raw tcp sockets without a networking framework
central server broadcasting across concurrent clients
clear separation of implemented and planned scope

title: Simple Rust Kernel
summary: Hobby OS kernel written in no-std Rust and run in QEMU
description: A hobby operating-system kernel written in Rust for x86_64 bare-metal execution. The project follows the core architecture introduced in Philipp Oppermann's OS-development series while incorporating independent additions and implementation choices as a practical study of kernel startup, hardware-facing code, and development without the standard library.

Cargo is configured through the Rust bootloader ecosystem to produce a bootable image and launch it directly in QEMU. A custom kernel-mode test runner executes integration and unit tests, reports results through the terminal, and exits the virtual machine correctly on success or failure.
highlights: x86_64 bare-metal execution with no-std rust
bootable image and qemu runner integrated with cargo
custom test runner for kernel-mode tests

title: Java DSA
summary: Classical data structures behind a custom generic interface hierarchy
description: A study and reference library that implements classical data structures and algorithms in Java instead of delegating to the standard collections framework. A custom generic hierarchy separates abstractions such as Collection, LinearCollection, List, and Stack from array-backed, singly linked, and doubly linked implementations. Keeping several representations behind shared contracts makes their memory, access, insertion, and traversal tradeoffs explicit while exercising reusable API design inspired by the Java Collections framework.
highlights: array-based and linked implementations side by side
generic interface hierarchy inspired by java collections
implementations keep underlying algorithms visible

title: RSS Server
summary: Early Go backend experiment using Goose migrations and sqlc
description: An unfinished RSS backend written in Go as an early exercise in service and database development. The repository established a database workflow using Goose for schema migrations and sqlc for type-safe query code, but it remained a work in progress and did not reach the complete feed-aggregation and serving scope described in the original portfolio note.
highlights: go backend development
goose database migrations
type-safe sql access generated with sqlc

title: Mathlib
summary: Small C++23 mathematics library with Make-based builds and tests
description: A compact C++23 mathematics library created to practice reusable numeric code and library organization. The repository separates library sources from tests, uses Make targets to build the library and test executable with GCC, and provides a focused environment for exploring mathematical types, operations, and modern C++ API design.
highlights: reusable numeric code in c++23
separate library and test targets
make-based gcc build workflow

title: Screenway
summary: Spring Boot cinema backend modeling screenings, bookings and payments
description: A learning-oriented backend that models the operation of a cinema network as a realistic Spring Boot application. Screenway covers cinemas, films, screenings, users, seat bookings, and payments, with PostgreSQL persistence and Docker-based local infrastructure. It was designed to practice domain modeling and transactional backend architecture and was archived before the wider expansion proposed in its README.
highlights: cinema booking and payment domain model
spring boot with postgresql persistence
containerized local infrastructure

title: Advent of Code
summary: Algorithmic puzzle solutions across three Advent of Code events
description: Solutions to the 2023, 2024, and 2025 Advent of Code programming events, written first in Python and then primarily in Rust. The exercises cover parsing irregular input, selecting appropriate data structures, implementing search and simulation algorithms, and balancing clarity with performance under puzzle-specific constraints. Separate annual repositories preserve the progression from general problem solving toward greater Rust fluency.
highlights: solutions spanning the 2023, 2024 and 2025 events
input parsing, algorithms, search and simulation
progression from python to primarily rust

title: Sudoker
summary: Command-line Sudoku generator and backtracking solver written in C++
description: A C++ command-line program that generates Sudoku grids and solves built-in or imported puzzles using optimized backtracking search. It validates imported fields, ignores non-grid formatting while parsing, lets users control how many values are prefilled during generation, and provides Make targets for optimized GCC builds. The project is a focused exercise in constraint solving, recursive search, input validation, and performance tuning; its README also documents a remaining edge-case limitation for some densely prefilled grids.
highlights: sudoku generation and recursive backtracking solver
custom grid import and validation
optimized command-line build with documented limitations

title: Minecraft Mods and Plugins
summary: Forge mods and Spigot plugins implementing custom Minecraft mechanics
description: A collection of Java projects built against the Minecraft Forge and Spigot APIs, including the Guncore mod and the Project-G and Item Asylum server plugins. The work spans custom items and gameplay mechanics, minigame and server-side logic, event-driven integrations, Gradle-based mod builds, and the practical constraints of extending a large third-party codebase. Most of the collection targeted Minecraft 1.12.2, while Guncore was later revisited on a newer branch.
highlights: custom forge mod items and gameplay mechanics
event-driven spigot server plugins and minigames
integration with large version-sensitive third-party apis

title: Synco
summary: Minimal Rust async runtime with a custom executor, wakers and proc macros
description: A from-scratch asynchronous runtime built to explore how Rust futures are scheduled beneath higher-level frameworks such as Tokio. Synco implements a task queue, spawner, executor, custom wakers, delayed futures, and a runtime that can block on asynchronous work using only the standard library for its core scheduling machinery.

A companion procedural-macro crate provides `#[synco::main]` and `#[synco::test]` entry points, while integration tests exercise the executor and runtime APIs. The project is intentionally small and experimental: its purpose is to make task scheduling, wake-up behavior, and runtime control flow visible rather than to replace a production async ecosystem.
highlights: custom future executor and task wake-up queue
delay future and blocking runtime implementation
procedural macros for async main functions and tests

title: C Smart Pointer Collection
summary: Reference-counted smart pointers and typed ownership helpers for C
description: A low-level C library that explores bringing explicit, reference-counted shared ownership to a language without native smart pointers. Its current `shared_ptr` implementation can copy values into a combined object-and-counter allocation or take ownership of an existing heap allocation, then tracks owners through explicit copy, move, validity, and release operations.

Macros generate type-specific pointer structures and wrapper functions over the generic implementation, while optional GCC and Clang cleanup attributes provide automatic scope-exit release. The Make-based project produces static and shared libraries, publishes Doxygen API documentation through GitHub Pages, and includes executable scenarios covering creation, copy chains, ownership transfer, reference-count changes, and final cleanup.
highlights: reference-counted shared ownership with copy and move operations
type-specific apis generated from generic c macros
optional automatic cleanup plus static and shared library builds

title: Win-Tools
summary: Native Windows implementations of ls, grep, head and touch
description: A collection of native Windows command-line utilities that brings familiar UNIX-style workflows to the platform through implementations of `ls`, `grep`, `head`, and `touch`. Each command is built directly on the Windows API rather than through a POSIX compatibility layer, keeping platform behavior, performance, and executable size under direct control.

The codebase evolved from C to primarily C++ to simplify ownership and reduce memory-safety risks while retaining low-level access to Win32. Visual Studio and MSBuild configurations produce 32-bit and 64-bit binaries that can be placed on `PATH` as native command replacements. The current goal is to stabilize and optimize the first four tools before expanding the collection.
highlights: built directly on the windows api without a posix layer
native implementations of ls, grep, head and touch
visual studio and msbuild targets for 32-bit and 64-bit binaries

title: Guitar Setup Skill
summary: Reusable agent skill for matching guitar and amplifier settings to a song
description: A reusable AI-agent skill that turns a target song and the player's available equipment into a practical guitar tone setup. It guides the agent through pickup selection, amplifier channel and EQ choices, gain and effects configuration, tone matching, and iterative refinement based on player feedback. A reusable template produces a per-user equipment reference so later recommendations remain grounded in the instruments, amplifier, pedals, and controls the player actually owns.
highlights: equipment-aware guitar and amplifier recommendations
structured tone-matching and feedback workflow
reusable per-user equipment reference template

title: Context Manager
summary: Agent skill for preserving engineering context across sessions and coding agents
description: An agent skill for preserving engineering context across long-running tasks, sessions, and coding agents. It creates a self-contained `.context/<ISSUE-ID>/` workspace for each issue, with durable sources of truth for scope and acceptance criteria, findings, attempted approaches, decisions from human conversations, related issues, and the next handoff action.

The skill keeps essential status easy to reconstruct without relying on a single chat history, while optional folders retain supporting research, source material, and attachments. It can scaffold issue workspaces through a bundled helper and is installable for Claude Code as well as other supported coding agents through `npx skills`. The repository includes an anonymized real-world BIOS investigation demonstrating months of iterative research and cross-session handoffs.
highlights: self-contained per-issue context workspace with explicit handoff state
durable records for scope, findings, attempts, conversations and related issues
works across long-running tasks, sessions and coding agents
